newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe finance markets open despite strike call.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe finance markets open despite strike call.

text.p: Zimbabwe's financial markets opened normally on Tuesday despite a call for a nationwide stoppage to press President Robert Mugabe's government to resolve a crippling strike by nurses and doctors.
"We're still trading as usual," one stock broker said.
The foreign exchange and local money markets were also trading normally at 0830 hours (0630 GMT), dealers said.

The Zimbabwe Congress of Trade Unions (ZCTU) representing workers from the private sector, called for a two-day strike starting on Tuesday to force the government to negotiate with junior doctors and nurses who went on strike three weeks ago demanding better salaries and working conditions.
